atcGroups.name: Systemic hormonal preparations, excluding sex hormones and insulins

areas.name: Cardiovascular
areas.summary: Medicines for blood pressure, heart failure, rhythm disorders, angina and cholesterol.

areas.name: Anticoagulants, antiplatelets & haematology
areas.summary: Medicines that prevent or treat clots, dissolve them, stop platelets sticking, replace iron and vitamins, stimulate blood-cell production or control bleeding.

areas.name: Diabetes
areas.summary: Insulins by duration of action, the non-insulin glucose-lowering classes, fixed-dose combinations and rescue products for hypoglycaemia.

areas.name: Thyroid, adrenal & hormonal
areas.summary: Replacement and suppression of thyroid, adrenal, pituitary and parathyroid hormones.

areas.name: Gastrointestinal
areas.summary: Acid, reflux and ulcer medicines, antiemetics, laxatives and antidiarrhoeals, inflammatory bowel disease therapies, pancreatic and liver products.

areas.name: Respiratory
areas.summary: Bronchodilators, inhaled and systemic anti-inflammatory medicines, biologics for severe asthma, cough and mucus medicines, pulmonary hypertension and cystic fibrosis therapies.

areas.name: Allergy
areas.summary: Antihistamines, nasal sprays, mast-cell stabilisers, decongestants, adrenaline for anaphylaxis, immunotherapy and biologics used in allergic disease.

areas.name: Pain & analgesia
areas.summary: Simple analgesics, anti-inflammatories, opioids and their antagonists, medicines for nerve pain, local anaesthetics and migraine treatments.

areas.name: Neurology
areas.summary: Antiseizure medicines, treatments for Parkinson disease, dementia, multiple sclerosis and migraine.

areas.name: Psychiatry
areas.summary: Antidepressants, anxiolytics and sedatives, antipsychotics, mood stabilisers, ADHD medicines and treatments for substance use.

areas.name: Anaesthetics & perioperative
areas.summary: Medicines used to numb, sedate and anaesthetise, relax muscles, reverse those effects and support the circulation around surgery.

areas.name: Antibiotics
areas.summary: Every major antibacterial class, systemic and topical.

areas.name: Antivirals
areas.summary: Medicines against herpesviruses, influenza, hepatitis B and C, HIV, SARS-CoV-2 and RSV.

areas.name: Antifungals
areas.summary: Systemic, topical and vaginal antifungal medicines by class.

areas.name: Antimycobacterials
areas.summary: Medicines for tuberculosis, drug-resistant tuberculosis, latent infection, leprosy and non-tuberculous mycobacteria.

areas.name: Antiparasitics
areas.summary: Antimalarials, antiprotozoals, anthelmintics and treatments for scabies and lice.

areas.name: Rheumatology & immunology
areas.summary: Disease-modifying drugs, targeted biologics and small molecules, gout medicines, immunoglobulins and the immunosuppressants used after transplantation.

areas.name: Oncology
areas.summary: Cytotoxic chemotherapy classes, hormonal therapies, targeted small molecules, antibodies, immunotherapies, cell therapies and supportive medicines. Oncology pages require stricter sourcing and review.

areas.name: Dermatology
areas.summary: Topical and systemic medicines for skin disease: corticosteroids, calcineurin and PDE4 inhibitors, retinoids, acne, psoriasis and eczema treatments, antifungals, hair and pigment therapies.

areas.name: Ophthalmic
areas.summary: Eye drops, ointments and injections: lubricants, anti-infectives, anti-inflammatories, allergy drops, pupil-acting drugs, glaucoma medicines and anti-VEGF injections.

areas.name: Ear, nose & throat
areas.summary: Ear drops, wax softeners, nasal sprays and throat preparations.

areas.name: Reproductive, gynaecology & obstetric
areas.summary: Contraception, hormone therapy, fertility drugs, endometriosis and fibroid treatments, medicines used in labour and pregnancy, vaginal anti-infectives and menopause therapies.

areas.name: Urology & men's health
areas.summary: Medicines for prostate enlargement, bladder symptoms, erectile dysfunction, urinary pain and testosterone replacement.

areas.name: Bone & osteoporosis
areas.summary: Medicines that slow bone loss or build bone, with the calcium and vitamin D that support them.

areas.name: Vaccines
areas.summary: Human vaccines by disease target: platform, antigen, combinations, age indication, route, formulation and current schedule references. Schedules change and are versioned from current authoritative guidance.

areas.name: Biologics
areas.summary: Medicines made by or from living cells. 'Biologic' is a product type, not a therapeutic class: each biologic also belongs to a therapeutic area.

areas.name: Gene & cell therapies
areas.summary: Advanced therapy medicinal products: gene replacement and editing, viral vectors, CAR-T and other engineered cells, stem-cell-derived products. Every entity requires current regulatory verification.

areas.name: Emergency & antidotes
areas.summary: Medicines used in resuscitation and poisoning. Dosing is never given here: emergency dosing must be sourced, jurisdiction-specific and medically reviewed.

areas.name: IV fluids, electrolytes & nutrition
areas.summary: Crystalloids, colloids, electrolyte replacements and parenteral or regulated enteral nutrition.

areas.name: Contrast & diagnostic agents
areas.summary: Substances given to make structures visible on imaging or to test a body function.

areas.name: Radiopharmaceuticals
areas.summary: Radioactive medicines for imaging (diagnostic) and treatment (therapeutic): isotope, targeting mechanism, use, route, the related imaging or procedure and radiation-specific precautions.

routes.name: Buccal
routes.summary: Held against the inside of the cheek.

routes.name: Topical
routes.summary: Applied to the skin or a surface.

routes.name: Transdermal
routes.summary: Absorbed through the skin from a patch or gel into the bloodstream.

routes.name: Nebulised
routes.summary: Breathed in as a mist from a nebuliser.

routes.name: Intravenous
routes.summary: Injected or infused into a vein.

routes.name: Intraosseous
routes.summary: Into the bone marrow, an emergency alternative to a vein.

routes.name: Intrathecal
routes.summary: Into the fluid around the spinal cord.

routes.name: Epidural
routes.summary: Into the space outside the membranes of the spinal cord.

routes.name: Intravitreal
routes.summary: Into the jelly of the eye.

routes.name: Intracameral
routes.summary: Into the front chamber of the eye.

routes.name: Implant
routes.summary: Placed under the skin or in a tissue to release the medicine over months.

routes.name: Local infiltration
routes.summary: Injected into the tissue to be numbed or treated.

routes.name: Enteral tube
routes.summary: Given through a feeding tube into the stomach or intestine.

productTypes.name: Small-molecule medicine
productTypes.summary: A chemically synthesised medicine, the majority of tablets, capsules and injections.

productTypes.name: Biologic
productTypes.summary: A medicine made by or from living cells: antibodies, recombinant proteins, enzymes, cytokines, clotting factors, immunoglobulins. A product type, not a therapeutic class.

productTypes.name: Biosimilar
productTypes.summary: A biologic shown to be highly similar to an already licensed reference biologic.

productTypes.name: Monoclonal antibody
productTypes.summary: An antibody engineered to bind one target (names ending in -mab).

productTypes.name: Recombinant protein or hormone
productTypes.summary: A human protein made by engineered cells: insulins, growth hormone, erythropoietins, enzymes, clotting factors.

productTypes.name: Vaccine
productTypes.summary: A product that trains the immune system against a disease target.

productTypes.name: Blood-derived product
productTypes.summary: Immunoglobulins, albumin, clotting-factor concentrates and other products prepared from blood or plasma.

productTypes.name: Gene therapy
productTypes.summary: A product that adds, replaces or edits genetic material in a person's cells.

productTypes.name: Cell therapy
productTypes.summary: Living cells given as treatment: CAR-T cells, other engineered immune cells, stem-cell-derived products.

productTypes.name: Radiopharmaceutical
productTypes.summary: A radioactive medicine used for imaging (diagnostic) or treatment (therapeutic).

productTypes.name: Contrast agent
productTypes.summary: A substance given to make blood vessels, organs or cavities show up on imaging.

productTypes.name: Diagnostic agent
productTypes.summary: A dye, tracer or challenge substance used in a test rather than as treatment.

productTypes.name: Intravenous fluid
productTypes.summary: Crystalloid or colloid solutions given into a vein.

productTypes.name: Electrolyte preparation
productTypes.summary: Potassium, magnesium, calcium, phosphate or bicarbonate preparations.

productTypes.name: Herbal medicine or supplement
productTypes.summary: A product regulated as a herbal medicine or supplement rather than a licensed medicine.

productTypes.name: Other product type
productTypes.summary: A product that fits none of the other types.

regulatoryStatuses.name: Prescription only
regulatoryStatuses.summary: Supplied only against a prescription (UK POM, US Rx-only).

regulatoryStatuses.name: Over the counter
regulatoryStatuses.summary: Sold without a prescription in general retail (UK GSL).

regulatoryStatuses.name: Pharmacy or behind the counter
regulatoryStatuses.summary: Sold without a prescription but only from a pharmacy, under a pharmacist's supervision (UK P).

regulatoryStatuses.name: Controlled substance
regulatoryStatuses.summary: Additional legal controls on prescribing, supply and possession (UK Misuse of Drugs schedules, US DEA schedules); always in addition to prescription status.

regulatoryStatuses.name: Specialist or restricted
regulatoryStatuses.summary: Prescribed only by, or on the advice of, a specialist, or within a restricted-access programme.

regulatoryStatuses.name: Hospital only
regulatoryStatuses.summary: Supplied and administered only in hospital.

regulatoryStatuses.name: Emergency-use authorisation
regulatoryStatuses.summary: Authorised under an emergency or conditional mechanism rather than a full licence.

regulatoryStatuses.name: Discontinued
regulatoryStatuses.summary: No longer marketed in the jurisdiction, though the licence may remain.

regulatoryStatuses.name: Withdrawn
regulatoryStatuses.summary: Licence withdrawn or suspended, usually for safety reasons.

regulatoryStatuses.name: Investigational
regulatoryStatuses.summary: Not licensed; available only in clinical trials or on a named-patient basis.
